counterexample: Lemma 1 is false, so no repair of line 0052 is possible. Let n >= 8 be even, alpha = 1/4, and let G consist of a clique on n-1 vertices plus one isolated vertex v. For any S with |S| = n/2 >= 4, S contains at least n/2 - 1 >= 3 clique vertices, so N(S) = V \ {v} and |N(S)| = n - 1 >= n/2 + n/4 (equivalent to n >= 4). Hence G satisfies the expansion hypothesis with alpha = 1/4, yet delta(G) = deg(v) = 0, which is not > alpha*n. The same graph shows the derived inequality alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n at line 0051 is satisfied, not violated, so line 0052's claimed contradiction is vacuous. (Separately, G = K_n satisfies the hypothesis with alpha = 1/2, refuting the strict claim alpha < 1/2 at line 0019.)
reasoning_summary: 0001-0009 verbatim restatement of the problem; no claim, nothing to check. 0010-0015 Theorem 1 restates the hypothesis and goal faithfully (note n/2 forces n even, and since k is arbitrary and may exceed n, 'path' must be read as a walk; this reading is used below). 0016-0017 proof plan (min-degree lemma, then greedy extension) is coherent. 0018 Lemma 1 states delta(G) > alpha*n -- this claim is in fact FALSE under the stated hypothesis (see counterexample), though the failure only becomes visible at 0052. 0019-0021 asserts alpha < 1/2 with the justification that |N(S)| >= n/2 + alpha*n >= n is 'impossible': faulty, since |N(S)| >= n is attainable with N(S) = V (K_n satisfies the hypothesis with alpha = 1/2); the hypothesis only yields alpha <= 1/2. This slip is non-load-bearing (every later use needs only alpha <= 1/2), so I do not treat it as the fatal step. 0022-0023 contradiction hypothesis deg(v) <= alpha*n is a legitimate proof-by-contradiction setup. 0024-0025 |N[v]| = deg(v) + 1 <= alpha*n + 1 is correct. 0026-0027 |U| = n - deg(v) - 1 >= (1-alpha)n - 1 is correct arithmetic. 0028-0030 |U| > n/2 - 1 follows from alpha < 1/2 for every n (the appeal to 'sufficiently large n' is unnecessary but harmless; under the correct bound alpha <= 1/2 one still gets |U| >= n/2 - 1, which is all that is needed). 0031-0032 choosing T subset of U with |T| = n/2 - 1 and setting S = {v} u T with |S| = n/2 is valid since v is not in U and |U| >= n/2 - 1. 0033-0034 N(S) = N(v) u N(T) holds by definition of neighborhood of a set. 0035 correct: u in T subset V\N[v] implies u not adjacent to v. 0036-0037 correct: V\{v} = N(v) u U disjointly, and N(u) subset V\{v}, so N(u) subset N(v) u U. 0038-0041 the union over u in T inherits the inclusion N(T) subset N(v) u U: correct. 0044-0045 N(S) subset N(v) u U: correct combination of 0034 and 0041. 0046-0047 N(v) and U are disjoint, so |N(S)| <= deg(v) + (n - deg(v) - 1) = n - 1: correct. 0048-0051 combining with the hypothesis gives n/2 + alpha*n <= n - 1, i.e. alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n: correct algebra, but note this is a weak, satisfiable bound. 0052-0053 FIRST FATAL FAILURE: the claim that 'for any fixed alpha > 0 and sufficiently large n this inequality is violated' is backwards -- 1/2 - 1/n increases to 1/2, so for fixed alpha < 1/2 the inequality alpha <= 1/2 - 1/n HOLDS for all large n; no contradiction is obtained and Lemma 1 is not proved. The gap is not patchable: the clique K_{n-1} plus an isolated vertex satisfies the hypothesis with alpha = 1/4 and has minimum degree 0, so Lemma 1 is false as stated. Crucially, the derived bound |N(S)| <= n - 1 never depended on deg(v) being small, so the argument could never yield a contradiction. 0054 statement of an inductive construction: fine as a plan. 0055 base case v1 in W1 is valid since |W1| >= (1-alpha)n > 0. 0056-0058 induction hypothesis and the goal of the inductive step are stated correctly. 0059-0060 |complement of W_{i+1}| = n - |W_{i+1}| <= alpha*n: correct. 0061-0062 the counting |N(v_i) n W_{i+1}| >= |N(v_i)| - |complement| > alpha*n - alpha*n = 0 is arithmetically correct BUT rests entirely on |N(v_i)| > alpha*n, i.e. on the unproved and false Lemma 1; hence this step is unjustified (and in the isolated-vertex example v_i could have degree 0). 0063-0064 the selection of v_{i+1} in N(v_i) n W_{i+1} is valid given 0062's nonemptiness, so it inherits 0062's defect. 0065 the induction is formally correct given the inductive step, and under the walk reading forced by arbitrary k there is no additional distinctness obligation; but since 0062 fails, the conclusion is not established. 0066 page number. Overall: the proof breaks at line 0052, where a non-contradiction is declared a contradiction, and the lemma it purports to establish is actually false, so the path/walk construction at 0061-0062 has no valid foundation.
